Game Genie, compare $CD: RET over the hit check $01:4837 (same address in both). tools/gb1/test_cheats.lua, random-input bot 6,000 frames from 1-1: 0 hits with the code, 7 hits / 7 lost sets without. GameShark: player +$4F (the after-hit flash flag) = 1 and its counter +$49 = 0, so $01:4866 always reports the flash; same bot: 0 hits (jp and wario).

effect: Win every normal set at once (stage clear; not boss sets)
note: GameShark: the three enemy object pages' state bytes $C100/$C200/$C300 forced to 0, so $01:487E sees all enemies gone and the set ends won ($C590 = 2). With the invincibility code: 6 sets won and 1-1 to 1-4 in 6,000 frames; boss sets don't end with it (the 1-boss waits; $01:48C7 needs the boss itself, $C3F7 = 1). GB1 has no lives: a lost match goes to the continue screen. Game Genie: $01:488A OR A -> XOR A, so the enemy check sees every page empty; with C98-37B-D5D: 12 sets won, 1-1 to 1-4 in 6,000 frames (jp and wario).

code: Win 240 rounds of the extra battle (5656; Wario Blast 6565 as Wario)
effect: PERFECT! ENEMY 240 screen with a fixed CODE -SVJV-, then CONGRATULATIONS!
note: After each round the extra battle ($00:35A4) calls $0A:4EFC (Wario $0A:5398), which checks the defeat count $C1D1-$C1D3 (one decimal digit per byte); at 240 it jumps to $0A:4DFF (Wario $0A:528B), which draws PERFECT! / ENEMY 240 / CODE -SVJV- / CONGRATULATIONS! (tile map $08:40D2); A or Start goes back to the title. The code is the same in both carts, likely a contest proof code. In Mesen (JP): the count set to 239 during the battle, one more round won, and the screen came up.

effect: The extra battle's 240-win PERFECT! screen at once (turn on after the 5656 / 6565 code is accepted)
note: GameShark: the defeat count $C1D1-$C1D3 held at 2-4-x, so the first check after a round sees 240+. $C1D1-$C1D3 is also the password digit buffer, so switch the codes on only after the password is accepted, then press A on the GREAT BATTLE intro. Tested in Mesen on both carts.

effect: Japan plays the attract story after about 36 seconds; Wario Blast stays on the title
note: Japan's title loop counts BC = $3C20 down ($0A:40A7-$40B7) and then jumps to the story ($0A:4106). Wario Blast's loop ($0A:40AA-$40E1) has no counter, as the story is gone. In Mesen with no input: Japan showed the story 36 s after the title, Wario Blast was still on the title at 56 s. Image: Japan (top) and Wario Blast at the title, +36 s and +56 s.

effect: Two tunes the game never plays
note: Music goes through the request byte $C3F1 (CALL $0AC4). The game asks for 00-06 and 0B as constants and 09-12 from the stage table at $00:1F04 (Wario $1E99). The song table at $07:4A0E has 00-12, and 07 and 08 have channel data of their own but no request. 07 is about 11 s, loud, and doesn't loop; 08 is about 11 s, quiet and rhythmic, and doesn't loop either. Recorded in BizHawk.
